about: I grew up playing marble games on bare ground: a line drawn with a stick, a small hole, a handful of marbles, and no rulebook. The rules lived in our heads and changed a little from street to street. I made this game to bring those afternoons back.

Nothing here is invented from nothing. Each mode starts with a game people really played: the toss at the hole that decided who went first, the three-hole race, and the game of the line, the hole, the stake and the marble you must not touch. I use the words those games use. Where you grew up, the line, the hole or the game itself may have another name.

I changed some rules so the games work well on a phone. Those are my decisions, not the tradition's. The game scatters the marbles for you, a marble that leaves the play area is put back, and bonus shots and turns have limits so a game always ends. In Guli Khela every side pays the stake, a fine is one marble that the game sets down for you, and giving up ends the match with you last. In Batto, a marble that finishes leaves the ground, a first toss that lands in the first hole counts as reaching it, and a marble resting in a hole is shot from the edge of the hole.
It is not an official or complete rulebook, and it does not claim to be how the game was played everywhere. If you remember it differently, you are not wrong. Your way might be the one I never saw.
If you know these games, I would like to hear how you played them: the names you used, the distances, what happened when someone missed.
how_to_play: Press your marble and drag away from where you want it to go, like a slingshot. The arrow shows the direction and a longer pull means more power. Release to shoot. Pull back to the start to cancel.
Drag empty ground to turn the view, scroll or pinch to zoom, and use the buttons at the bottom to change view or reset it. The camera never changes your shot.
Toss a marble from behind the line toward the hole. A marble resting in the hole scores 3. Of the rest, the closest scores 2 and the next closest 1. After five rounds the highest total wins.

Everyone tosses once toward the first hole, and the closest goes first. Then each side shoots its own marble from where it lies (from the edge of the hole, if it rests in one), going from the first hole to the second, the third, and back to the first. Reach the hole you are heading for, or hit a rival's marble, and you shoot again (up to three extra shots in a turn). The last one to finish loses.

Every side pays a stake of marbles and tosses toward the hole. The closest side scatters the stake round the hole, and everyone else gets one attempt in turn. First tap the marble you must not touch: the baad. Then throw your marble. Touch exactly one other marble, and not the baad, and you win the dan and every marble on the ground. Touch the baad, or more than one marble, and you pay a fine of one marble from your purse, which stays on the ground. Touch nothing and your attempt is over. If nobody wins in three passes, the side that scattered keeps the ground. A side that cannot pay the next stake is out. Pause the match to surrender.
One dan of Guli Khela, for a few minutes. The same stake, scatter, baad and fines, and the match ends when the dan is won.
